definition: A chip designed specifically to accelerate AI workloads — GPUs, TPUs, NPUs, and custom ASICs — delivering the matrix throughput modern models demand.
details: A chip designed specifically to accelerate AI workloads — GPUs, TPUs, NPUs, and custom ASICs — delivering the matrix throughput modern models demand.

explainer.lead: An AI processor is a chip built to run artificial-intelligence calculations efficiently, especially the large matrix operations used by modern models. The category includes GPUs, TPUs, NPUs, and custom ASICs, and matters because these chips supply the throughput demanding AI workloads require.

tiers.eli5: Think of an AI model as a student doing an enormous number of similar maths problems. An AI processor is like a classroom full of calculators working together, so the model can finish much faster than with one calculator doing everything in turn.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use AI processors to accelerate model workloads, with GPUs, TPUs, NPUs, and custom ASICs representing different implementations of the same broad idea. The key consideration is whether the chip provides the matrix throughput required by the target workload, rather than treating every processor labelled “AI” as interchangeable.
tiers.paperLevel: An AI processor is application-oriented hardware designed to accelerate AI workloads, particularly matrix computations such as Y = XW, where X contains activations and W contains model weights. It is a category spanning GPUs, TPUs, NPUs, and custom ASICs, not a single fixed microarchitecture or performance metric.

explainer.example: Suppose a model computes Y = XW, where X is a matrix of input activations and W is a matrix of learned weights. An AI processor accelerates this matrix multiplication and returns Y for use by the next stage of the model.

usedIn.name: GPUs
usedIn.detail: Graphics processors included in the AI-processor category when used to accelerate AI workloads.

usedIn.name: TPUs
usedIn.detail: A processor family designed for the computational demands of AI.

usedIn.name: NPUs
usedIn.detail: Neural-processing units built to accelerate AI calculations.

usedIn.name: Custom ASICs
usedIn.detail: Special-purpose chips designed around particular AI acceleration requirements.

explainer.intuition: Modern AI models repeatedly perform large matrix calculations, so a chip optimized for that work can deliver more useful throughput than hardware designed primarily for general-purpose tasks. “AI processor” names the shared purpose of several chip families, not one universal design.
howItWorks: An AI workload presents calculations required by a model.
Much of the work is expressed as operations on matrices.
The AI processor executes those operations with hardware designed for AI acceleration.
The resulting matrix outputs feed subsequent model calculations.
High matrix throughput allows the overall workload to be processed efficiently.
explainer.whyItMatters: Modern models demand substantial matrix throughput, and processors designed for AI workloads provide hardware aimed directly at that demand. This makes AI processors a central part of the computing foundation on which those models run.
misconceptions: An AI processor is not one specific chip design; the term covers GPUs, TPUs, NPUs, and custom ASICs.
A GPU is not exclusively an AI processor, but it belongs to the category when used to accelerate AI workloads.
The term describes acceleration hardware, not an AI model or algorithm itself.
